steps.label: Fibrous roots
lines: Fibrous roots: a cluster of thin roots that
arises from the base of the stem after the
Ex: monocots such as wheat and paddy.
steps.why: The scoring fact is the origin: fibrous roots come from the BASE OF THE STEM, and only after the seed's radicle has died.
common_mistakes: Writing that fibrous roots grow from the radicle. They appear because the radicle degenerates.
steps.memory_tip: Fibrous = from the foot of the stem, after the radicle fails.
steps.margin_note: One origin line and one example per side; a small two-column table also works.

steps.label: Adventitious roots

lines.text: Adventitious roots arise from any part of

lines: the plant other than the radicle.
Ex: prop roots of banyan; roots of grasses
steps.why: Adventitious is defined by exclusion - any origin EXCEPT the radicle. That one phrase is the whole definition.
common_mistakes: Treating the two as opposites. Fibrous roots also arise outside the radicle, so they are adventitious in origin - the question asks how the terms differ, not which plant has which.
steps.memory_tip: Adventitious = arriving at an unusual place - anywhere but the radicle.
steps.margin_note: The phrase 'other than the radicle' is the mark; add one example.
